abstract:
DNA in CpG context is often epigenetically modified in vertebrate genomes which increases their mutation rate. However, it remains challenging to identify sample-specific CpG loci for analysis of epigenetic modifications. Here, we present a read-based likelihood framework for identifying reference and non-reference CpG loci with high precision and sensitivity in single-molecule long-read sequencing data from Nanopore and PacBio platforms. Including all sample-specific CpG loci increases the number of analyzable loci and reduces bias in modification level estimates, both critical factors for accurate analyses of epigenetic modifications.
The likelihood framework is implemented in the R package bsseq with the source code available on github https://github.com/hansenlab/bsseq. Installation instructions and a user guide for long-read analysis and likelihood-based filtering of CpG loci are available on Bioconductor https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/bsseq.html.
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
